title: Enterprise Onboarding, Integration & QBR Playbook
author: Priya Rao
body:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference customer-success and support best practices for enterprise onboarding, integration guidance, escalation procedures, known issues & workarounds, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) materials. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers, Support Engineers, and Account Owners who run enterprise onboarding and post-onboarding health checks.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-production request for enterprise customers to under 2 weeks for standard integrations.
- Ensure consistent escalation handling and SLA adherence.
- Provide a repeatable QBR cadence to review adoption, cost, and reliability metrics.

Scope:
- Applies to all Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) enterprise customers and self-serve customers that have signed an enterprise contract.
- Does not replace incident response runbooks for critical P0 outages; it augments those with customer facing steps.

Roles & ownership:
- CSM (owner): overall onboarding success, QBR scheduling, customer satisfaction.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): technical integration, API key provisioning, initial test calls, performance tuning.
- Support Engineer (SRE/Support): triage production incidents, apply workarounds, escalate to Eng teams.
- Account Executive (AM): contract and billing coordination.

Onboarding Playbook (step-by-step):
1) Pre-onboarding (owner: CSM)
   - Confirm contract type (Hosted / Dedicated / Private), region requirements, and compliance needs (e.g., SOC2, PCI, HIPAA).
   - Collect points of contact: primary technical lead, security lead, network admin, procurement.
   - Share onboarding plan and calendar (kickoff within 3 business days).

2) Kickoff (owner: CSM + SE)
   - Agenda: introductions, scope, success criteria, milestones, risk areas.
   - Deliverables: Access matrix, data residency confirmation, required IP allowlists, and SSO/KMS details.

3) Environment & Access (owner: SE)
   - Hosted: create tenant, provision API keys, set RBAC roles.
   - Dedicated/Private: coordinate infra runbook with eng-private-deployments (see related pages).
   - Document: service endpoints, key rotation policy, and monitoring hooks.

4) Integration & Validation (owner: SE)
   - Provide API quickstart and sample calls. Validate 3 test flows: auth, generation/chat, embeddings.
   - Example curl (hosted):
     curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate 
       -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" 
       -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
       -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0", "input":"Hello world"}'

   - Validate TLS, client IP allowlist, and proxy settings. Collect early success metrics (latency, error rate).

5) Performance Tuning (owner: SE + SRE)
   - Run baseline perf tests (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec) using the benchmarking suite.
   - Apply recommended batching and caching profiles from Redwood Optimize. Document chosen quantization profile if applicable.

6) Security & Compliance Review (owner: Security liaison + CSM)
   - Confirm KMS integration, audit logging, and data retention settings. Ensure compliance checklist is signed off.

7) Production Cutover (owner: CSM + SE)
   - Validate canary traffic (1–5% production) for 24–72 hours. Monitor KPIs: latency, error rate, token cost.
   - Full rollout only after canary SLOs are met.

8) Post-Cutover Monitoring & Handover (owner: CSM + Support)
   - Provide runbook for first 30 days: escalation contacts, normal operating thresholds, and maintenance windows.

Integration Guide (common items):
- API keys: Provisioned via Console > Security > API keys. Keys must be rotated every 90 days (recommended).
- Network: Provide customer IPs to add to Redwood allowlist for Dedicated; for Private deployments, confirm peering/VPN details.
- Observability: Install tracing hooks (X-Request-ID), configure log shipping (S3/CloudLogging) and metrics export (Prometheus/Grafana).
- Rate limits & quotas: Defaults: 60 rps per tenant for Hosted; Dedicated customers get configured limits per contract.
- Sample SDK snippet (pseudocode):
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=\"<API_KEY>\")
  resp = client.generate(model=\"redwood-1.0\", prompt=\"Summarize...\")
  assert resp.status == 200

Escalation Playbook (customer-facing):
- Severity definitions (customer-facing):
  - P0 / Sev 1: Complete production outage impacting all users. Target response: initial contact within 15 minutes, on-call mobilized.
  - P1 / Sev 2: Major degradation (e.g., 50% error rate or p95 latency > 3x typical). Target response: initial contact within 1 hour.
  - P2 / Sev 3: Partial impact or isolated errors. Target response: initial contact within 4 business hours.
  - P3 / Minor: Non-urgent questions or feature requests. Response within 48 business hours.

Escalation steps (internal):
1) Triage (Support): confirm customer, system timestamps, request ids, and relevant logs.
2) Contain (Support/SRE): apply temporary workarounds (route to model variant, scale up dedicated pool, disable bad prompt set).
3) Escalate to Eng (if needed): open an internal incident with summary, reproducer, and perf traces. Include SLO breach risk.
4) Communicate (CSM): provide customer with timeline and status updates every 30 minutes for P0, hourly for P1.
5) Post-incident review: Support + Eng + CSM produce a technical postmortem and customer-facing summary within 72 hours for P0/P1.

Contact matrix:
- Support (first line): support@redwood.example (or portal ticket).
- On-call SRE (pager): +1-555-0100 (use internal rota).
- SE escalation: se@redwood.example.

Known issues & workarounds (selected):
- Issue: Elevated tokenization errors when input contains unescaped control characters.
  Workaround: Sanitize input by stripping control characters or run pre-tokenize validation.

- Issue: p99 latency spike when KV cache warms on long-context workloads.
  Workaround: Pre-warm KV cache with representative prompts during canary; use caching policy 'prefix-only' for inference-heavy paths.

- Issue: Occasional 429 throttles when burst traffic exceeds rate limits.
  Workaround: Apply client-side exponential backoff with jitter and request quota increases for Dedicated customers via support.

- Issue: Private deployment healthcheck failing after certificate rotation.
  Workaround: Confirm cert bundles on all nodes were rotated; run the cert-sync script from onprem-packaging runbook and restart the health agent.

(Representative table for operational thresholds):
| Metric | Target | Alert threshold | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| p99 latency (inference) | < 800ms | > 1200ms | SRE |
| 5m error rate | < 0.5% | > 2% | Support |
| Token cost / 1k tokens | Baseline by contract | 20% above baseline | CSM/Finance |

Support Process (ticket lifecycle):
- Ticket intake: Portal/email -> Support triage within SLA window.
- Ownership: Support owns initial triage until issue is reproduced or determined to be SE/Eng work.
- Escalation: Create internal incident and link ticket (include logs, request IDs, customer impact).
- Resolution & closure: Provide remediation steps and restore service; include timeline and root cause when available.
- Follow-up: For P0/P1 incidents, schedule customer-facing debrief and include action plan.

Health Checks & QBR Materials:
- Monthly health check checklist (CSM):
  - Active users & usage trends (30/60/90 day).
  - API error rate & latency trends (p50/p95/p99).
  - Cost efficiency: tokens per session and cost per 1k tokens.
  - Model quality: sample prompt regression checks; any quality alerts from Redwood Optimize.
  - Security posture: audit log review, key rotations performed.

- Quarterly Business Review (QBR) template (CSM + AM):
  - Slide 1: Executive summary (usage, spend, top wins).
  - Slide 2: Reliability & performance (uptime, major incidents, mitigation).
  - Slide 3: Adoption & product usage patterns (top routes, models).
  - Slide 4: Cost & optimization opportunities (batching, quantization, routing).
  - Slide 5: Roadmap & planned improvements (product features, dedicated capacity changes).
  - Slide 6: Action items & success metrics for next quarter.

Sample QBR agenda (60 minutes):
- 0–5 min: Welcome & Objectives (CSM)
- 5–20 min: Usage & Adoption deep dive (CSM/SE)
- 20–35 min: Reliability & Ops review (SRE/Support)
- 35–50 min: Optimization & roadmap (Product/SE)
- 50–60 min: Action items and next steps (CSM/AM)

Templates & artifacts to attach to customer QBR:
- Monthly health check report (CSV/JSON export of metrics).
- Incident summary deck for any P0/P1 in the quarter.
- Proposed optimization plan with estimated cost savings.

Operational SLAs & SLOs (customer-facing summary):
- Response SLAs: P0: 15 min initial response; P1: 1 hour; P2: 4 hours.
- Uptime SLO (Dedicated): 99.9% monthly.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 600ms for standard generation workloads (contract-defined).

Related pages: [enterprise-onboarding-and-support-playbook], [enterprise-onboarding-escalation-playbook-2025], [integration-guides/hosted-api-quickstart].

Appendices:
- Appendix A: Quick checklist for CSMs (one-pager).
- Appendix B: Support escalation form (fields to capture: impact, workflow, logs, example requests).
- Appendix C: Contact matrix (on-call schedule link).

Change log:
- 2024-11-01: Initial draft (Priya Rao).
- 2025-02-15: Added QBR template, updated severity response windows, added known issue on tokenization errors (reviewers: Marcus Chen, Elena Garcia).

If you are running an onboarding now and need the playbook run by a Solutions Engineer, create a ticket with subject: "Onboarding request - <CustomerName> - <AccountID>" and tag the SE rotation alias.
